question: Under the Liberalisation Policy, a lot of industries were reserved for the public sector. Which of the following industries are still reserved under public sector?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Atomic and Railway Operations**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Atomic and railway operations are strategically important sectors for national security and infrastructure, hence they are reserved for the public sector.
 
• The government maintains control over these sectors to ensure consistent and regulated management.
 
• Atomic energy involves sensitive technology and materials, requiring strict government oversight.
 
• Railway operations are crucial for national connectivity and economic stability, thus remaining under government control ensures reliability and safety.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Liberalisation Policy:**

 
 
• The Liberalisation Policy in India, initiated in 1991, aimed to open up the economy by reducing government regulations and restrictions on business operations.
 
• It involved measures like deregulation of industries, reduction of import tariffs, and the encouragement of foreign investment.
 
• The policy shift was aimed at increasing economic growth, improving efficiency, and integrating India into the global economy.
 
• Despite liberalisation, certain key sectors were retained under public sector control for strategic and security reasons.
 
 
 
• **Public Sector:**
 
 
• The public sector comprises enterprises and services owned and operated by the government.
 
 
• **Atomic Energy Sector:**
 
 
• The atomic energy sector involves the development and management of nuclear power and technology.
 
 
• **Railway Operations:**
 
 
• Railway operations refer to the management and operation of the railway network, including passenger and freight services.
